item.title: Inverse Modeling for Laser Pulse Shape Design in Inertial Confinement Fusion
item.description: arXiv:2610.33096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The achievement of practical fusion energy remains one of the most pressing unsolved scientific challenges, with immense implications for carbon-free power. A critical factor in the success of Inertial Confinement Fusion (ICF) is the design of a Laser Pulse Shape (LP) that can optimally drive implosions under stringent physical constraints. Traditional LP design relies on computationally expensive simulations and manual iterative refinement. We introduce the ICF Laser Pulse Shape Design System (LPDS), a generative inverse modeling framework that maps desired outcomes and target pellet configurations directly to optimized LPs. Crucially, we design a multi-objective loss function to ensure the generated LPs satisfy fundamental physical constraints and experimental requirements. Furthermore, we present constraint-conditioning, inpainting, and gradient-based LP editing mechanisms for fine-grained control over specific pulse characteristics during generation. Moreover, we study the transfer of our framework to a limited set of real experimental shots. Our method establishes a data-driven inverse design framework for LP design in ICF, contributing to the advancement of practical and sustainable fusion energy.

item.title: IRON-Meme: A Benchmark for Structured Understanding of Identities and Roles in Online Meme Narratives
item.description: arXiv:2610.33097v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As polarization grows on social media, understanding how political memes shape online narratives has become increasingly important. Previous research has relied on either qualitative frameworks that are hard to scale or computational methods that lack theoretical grounding. Both approaches treat narrative categories in isolation and focus exclusively on moral portrayals of identity. To address these limitations, we introduce a framework grounded in social science theories, encompassing three categories: social identities (such as gender, politics, and ethnicity), viewpoints (ingroup and outgroup perspectives), and narrative roles (moral character, intelligence, status, and power). Building on this framework, we present IRON-Meme, a human-annotated benchmark comprising 1,110 political memes across substantially more templates than existing benchmarks. Our analysis of IRON-Meme shows that most memes assign derogatory roles and that identities, roles, and templates are systematically interconnected. Evaluation of nine vision-language models indicates that frontier-scale and reasoning models achieve the highest performance, while accuracy on social identities and narrative roles decreases for less frequent labels. Incorporating template background knowledge does not enhance narrative role classification, suggesting that meme interpretation relies on how memes are adapted for specific communicative purposes. We make IRON-Meme and our code publicly available.

item.title: Prospect Theory in Large Language Models: A Meta-Analysis of Loss Aversion, Diminishing Sensitivity, and Probability Weighting
item.description: arXiv:2610.33103v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prospect theory splits risky choice into three parts: loss aversion, measured by the relative weight of losses to gains, $\lambda$ (e.g., $\lambda = 2$ implies that losses weigh twice as much as gains), diminishing sensitivity to the size of outcomes (i.e., the curvature and linearity of the value function), and the nonlinear weighting of probabilities. I examined whether Large Language Models (LLMs) display the same properties as people by meta-analyzing 102 fitted estimates from 11 studies covering 32 language models. The three components emerge differently. Loss aversion is modest: the pooled $\lambda$ is 1.26 (95% CI 1.06 to 1.46), far below the strongest human meta-analytic estimate ($\lambda = 1.96$) and compatible with more conservative ones (1.07 and 1.31). Matched by design, LLMs are compatible with people when gains and losses are symmetric ($\lambda = 1.15$ against 1.07), but well below them when losses are smaller than gains (1.46 against 2.3), where human loss aversion is strongest. Value functions are close to linear rather than concave under the Tversky-Kahneman method (1.01, against a human value of 0.67), but more concave than in people under the Tanaka method (0.52, against 0.67), so diminishing sensitivity depends on how it is measured. Probability weighting shows a human-like inverse S shape ($\gamma = 0.81$ under Tversky-Kahneman and 0.84 under the Tanaka method), though on few studies. In sum, LLMs show little loss aversion and little diminishing sensitivity, but retain human-like probability distortion, yet these generalizations shift when looking at specific model families and fitting methods.

item.title: Artificial Intelligence in Mechanical Engineering: Foundations, Opportunities, Challenges, and Responsibilities
item.description: arXiv:2610.33105v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping mechanical engineering (ME), from modeling, simulation, and optimization to diagnostics, design, and technical communication. Drawing on a round-table at the 28th ABCM International Congress on Mechanical Engineering (COBEM 2025), this article presents a structured perspective for the Brazilian and international ME communities. Rather than an exhaustive survey, it examines how AI can enhance engineering practice without compromising scientific rigor. We distinguish statistical learning from human cognition and discuss the capabilities, limitations, and emerging agentic forms of AI. We then consider industrial adoption, workforce changes, and AI-assisted scientific discovery, alongside the energy and infrastructure demands of AI computation and their implications for sustainability and thermal management. The discussion emphasizes the integration of physical knowledge, structured reasoning, and domain expertise into AI systems, particularly in safety-relevant applications. Topics include physics-informed and hybrid learning, physically constrained modeling, validation, uncertainty quantification, and certification. We also examine educational, epistemological, and ethical challenges, including curriculum reform, human-agent collaboration, professional accountability, and the preservation of engineering knowledge. We conclude with principles for responsible AI adoption in ME: physical consistency, rigorous validation, explicit treatment of uncertainty, energy sustainability, human oversight, and ethical responsibility. AI should complement, not replace, engineering judgment.

item.title: Collaborative In-Context Learning for Indoor Radio Map Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2610.31702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Indoor radio map estimation (RME) is essential for wireless applications such as coverage planning, localization, and network deployment. However, most existing methods follow a supervised learning paradigm that requires costly labeled data and task-specific model training. Moreover, indoor environments involve privacy-sensitive information, such as building layouts and structures, that often cannot be centralized. To address these challenges, we make the first attempt to formulate indoor RME as a collaborative in-context learning (ICL) problem. We propose Poly-Ripple, a framework in which multiple clients perform ICL using large autoregressive vision models (LAVMs) without model updates. Each client is prompted by its private demonstrations and predicts the radio map for the same scene query. To capture the causal structure of wireless propagation outward from the transmitter (Tx), we adopt ripple-ordered autoregressive modeling. We further introduce importance-aware aggregation to exploit heterogeneous contextual knowledge distributed across clients under the context length constraint. We provide theoretical analysis and conduct extensive experiments on a public indoor RME benchmark. The experimental results show that Poly-Ripple consistently outperforms representative ICL baselines, while aligning with our theoretical analysis.

item.title: The Path to NDE 4.0: A Review of Algorithms, Techniques, and Strategies for Autonomous Inspection
item.description: arXiv:2610.31704v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-Destructive Inspection (NDI) is a cornerstone of modern quality assurance, critical for ensuring the safety and reliability of infrastructure and manufactured components without causing damage. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the current NDI landscape, analyzing the field through four distinct lenses, namely, computational algorithms, physical techniques, industrial applications, and research objectives. We synthesize a broad range of academic literature to illustrate the rapid evolution from manual, analog interpretation to a digitized, data-centric paradigm known as NDE 4.0. Our analysis highlights the dominance of ultrasound and visual inspection as primary physical techniques, while revealing a significant shift toward deep learning and generative models for automated defect recognition. Despite these technological strides, the industry faces critical bottlenecks, notably the scarcity of standardized open-access datasets and the "black box" nature of AI models, which hinders widespread adoption. By charting these developments and identifying key research gaps, such as the need for explainable AI (XAI) and standardized digital twin protocols, this review offers a strategic roadmap for future research. It concludes that the future of NDI research should focus on the successful integration of intelligent, autonomous fusion of inspection data with advanced sensor technologies into asset lifecycle management.

item.title: Does LeWorldModel Preserve Local Action Geometry?
item.description: arXiv:2610.31716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine how closely pretrained LeWorldModel (LeWM) reproduces the effects of small action changes. Using matched simulator and model responses, we measure action sensitivity with Gram matrices at three perturbation scales. Across nearly a thousand states from Reacher and OGBench Cube, the most sensitive action directions differ by median angles of about $36^\circ$ and $42^\circ$, respectively, at the smallest scale. Increasing the perturbation tenfold reduces median normalized Gram discrepancy by roughly 70\% on Reacher and 47\% on Cube. Geometry measured in pixels and embeddings varies more across scales than the chosen physical-state geometry. On held-out directions, environment Grams achieve median embedding response errors of 17\% and 28\%, compared with 26\% and 38\% for an isotropic reference with the same trace. LeWM's errors are higher at this scale. These findings support scale-specific evaluation of action sensitivity; its effect on control remains an open question.

item.title: Towards Adversarially Robust Multigraph Neural Networks for Financial Crime Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2610.31718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Financial transaction networks are naturally represented as multigraphs, where repeated transactions between the same pair of accounts are modeled as distinct edges. Recently proposed multigraph neural network architectures leverage this structure explicitly to achieve a strong performance on anti-money laundering (AML) tasks. However, their robustness to adversaries that manipulate transaction structures to evade detection remains largely unexplored. We present the first scalable framework for structural attacks and adversarial training of multigraph neural networks using node-edge incidence matrices, adapting projected gradient descent and projected randomized block coordinate descent methods to optimize structural perturbations over such matrices. We further introduce a cycle-based regularizer that penalizes changes in the global counts of directed 2- and 3-cycles, providing a structural measure of attack plausibility. Experiments on synthetic pattern-detection and realistic AML datasets show that our learned attacks substantially outperform non-learnable perturbation baselines in reducing detection performance (PR-AUC), while adversarial training consistently improves robustness against these attacks. These results demonstrate that multigraph neural networks are vulnerable to learned structural attacks and that adversarial training provides an effective defense. Our code is available at https://github.com/denheijmans/robust_multignn.

item.title: Chemistry-resolved disagreement between Materials Project-compatible PBE(+U) and r2SCAN stability verdicts in the GNoME materials database
item.description: arXiv:2610.33101v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GNoME's stability labels rest on a Materials Project-compatible GGA/GGA+U workflow. Its authors report that 84% of discovered binaries and ternaries retain a negative decomposition energy under r2SCAN and 86.8% of tested quaternaries remain stable on the r2SCAN hull. We resolve that aggregate by chemistry over the 139,541 GNoME materials released with r2SCAN recomputations, a subset the dataset authors selected rather than sampled, using cluster bootstrap intervals over 8,429 structural-prototype proxy clusters. The aggregate conceals a 26.7-point spread at fixed element count, from 4.0% [3.3, 4.7] for plain quaternary intermetallics (no lanthanide, no 3d metal) to 30.7% [27.7, 33.8] for lanthanide-free 3d-containing quaternary oxides, a pair identified post hoc against a prospectively fixed threshold. Under our reading of the release's "All" reference set the two cells sit at 14.5% and 37.4%, preserving a 22.9-point spread. Presence of a Materials Project Hubbard-U-list element is strongly associated with disagreement, conditional on the other covariates, in a model over all 139,541 materials (cluster-robust odds ratio 3.45 [3.13, 3.80]). Neither selective U application nor hull proximity explains the association away: disagreement stays elevated outside the U-treated regime, and a natural cubic spline in the continuous PBE decomposition energy moves the odds ratio in the 117,018-material model only from 3.53 to 3.43 [3.07, 3.83]. For allocating a verification budget, composition supplements hull proximity rather than replacing it: over held-out cluster splits at a 20% budget, the two together surface 45.8% of disagreements against 40.4% for hull distance alone. An exploratory comparison against previously catalogued materials changes direction between populations. We measure disagreement between two workflows, not accuracy.

item.title: On the Doppler Effect in Static Materials: Vortices and Black, White and Worm-Hole Like Wave Trajectories
item.description: arXiv:2610.33141v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate the Doppler effect in a static material. The effect is achieved with a network of thin waveguides whose lengths depend on the direction of travel, chosen to simulate the compression and expansion of the wave experienced by a source travelling with velocity $v$. Each edge of length $\ell$ becomes a pair of waveguides of lengths $\ell/(1\mp v/c)$, one for each direction of travel. On a lattice this gives the field pattern of a moving source. To demonstrate the effect, we design a vortex, an analogue black hole and wormhole.

item.title: Evolution of microstructure and crystallographic texture in a novel Zr-4Nb-2Al alloy during hot rotary swaging
item.description: arXiv:2610.33247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A multi-step induction-assisted hot rotary swaging route was developed for the novel dual-phase Zr-4Nb-2Al alloy to investigate the evolution of microstructure, crystallographic texture, and mechanical properties during sequential deformation. Phase-transformation temperatures determined by electrical resistivity measurements were used to select processing conditions in the single-phase $\beta$ field at 880{\deg}C and the $\alpha+\beta$ field at 780{\deg}C. Induction heating with thermographic temperature control enabled reduction of the initial 12 mm rod to 6.3 mm, corresponding to a total area reduction of 72%. Swaging in the $\beta$ field refined millimetre-sized prior-$\beta$ grains to approximately 100 $\mu$m, while subsequent cooling produced a fine lamellar $\alpha+\beta$ microstructure. Further deformation in the $\alpha+\beta$ field disrupted the lamellar structure, promoted globularisation and recrystallisation of the $\alpha$ phase, and refined the $\beta$ phase. The microstructural evolution was accompanied by a pronounced $\langle 11\bar{2}0\rangle_{\alpha}\parallel\mathrm{SD}$ fibre texture in the $\alpha$ phase, whereas the $\beta$ phase exhibited predominantly $\langle 110\rangle_{\beta}\parallel\mathrm{SD}$ together with a $\langle 111\rangle_{\beta}\parallel\mathrm{SD}$ component. The phase constitution remained comparatively stable, with approximately 12-15 wt.% retained $\beta$ throughout processing. Subsequent $\alpha+\beta$ swaging decreased the compressive yield strength from 1103 to 839 MPa while increasing plastic deformability, with a maximum fracture strain of 32%. Radial hardness heterogeneity was progressively eliminated. These results demonstrate that induction-assisted rotary swaging in selected phase fields provides an effective route for tailoring microstructure, texture, and mechanical response in dual-phase zirconium alloys.

item.title: Winding-Controlled Topological Descendants of Antialtermagnets
item.description: arXiv:2610.33252v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Odd-parity spin splitting constrains magnetic band crossings but does not determine their topological descendants. We show that the Chern contribution of an isolated inverted sector is controlled by the phase winding of its transverse mass pair: when the masses and tangential velocities reverse together, contributions from successive Dirac points add rather than cancel. This distinguishes topological winding from the polynomial degree labeling the magnetic parent. For specified complementary masses, periodic tetragonal $h$- and hexagonal $j$-wave models host eight and twelve same-chirality Weyl points on a momentum plane, with gapped-slice Chern numbers $|C|=4$ and $6$, respectively. A microscopic four-band $p$-wave model identifies an antiunitary obstruction to first-order transverse masses and demonstrates a symmetry-broken $C=1$ phase at quarter filling. First-principles calculations for the proposed coplanar spin-vortex texture of LaMnAu$_5$ reveal the $h$-wave nodal pattern, its anisotropic spin--orbit reconstruction, and a mirror-channel spectral response that reverses under opposite spin rotations. Together, these results distinguish the symmetry of an odd-parity magnetic parent from the mass structure controlling the topology of its descendants.

item.title: Polarized X-rays from table-top free-electron-driven van der Waals crystals
item.description: arXiv:2610.33774v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Polarized X-rays are essential for polarization-sensitive techniques such as X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy, magnetic microscopy, and fluorescence imaging. These techniques are crucial in the study of molecular and material dynamics, which are in turn central to driving the global transition to clean energy and sustainability through research in photovoltaics, catalysis and optoelectronics. Currently, polarized X-rays with tunable polarization and photon energy are available only in large facilities like synchrotrons. Here, we theoretically predict and experimentally demonstrate the generation of linearly polarized X-rays from free electron-driven van der Waals crystals, without the need for additional optical stages like polarizers. We show that precise, real-time control over the polarization can be achieved by simply re-orienting the van der Waals crystal. Furthermore, we show that a high degree of polarization can be achieved across all polarization angles - from perpendicular to in-plane - with intensities exceeding 10^9 photons s^(-1) sr^(-1) mA^(-1). Using our findings, we present a scheme for table-top XANES, achieving performance comparable to that of synchrotron facilities. In the process, we develop a new methodology for performing XANES using high-quality polarized X-rays with larger spectral linewidths, named ORIXANES (Orientation-controlled XANES). Our findings pave the way to greater accessibility and smaller carbon footprint for advanced X-ray modalities.

item.title: Suppression of Sedimentation in Polystyrene Microsphere Suspensions via Femtosecond Laser Irradiation
item.description: arXiv:2610.34232v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Micrometer-sized particles denser than their medium settle out of suspension within hours, and Brownian motion is too weak to prevent it. We report that femtosecond laser irradiation at 1030 nm slows this settling in suspensions of 8 um polystyrene microspheres in water, without altering the particles themselves. Suspensions at three concentrations were treated for up to 3 h under weak acoustic agitation or vigorous magnetic stirring, each with and without simultaneous irradiation, and the particles remaining in the probe volume were quantified optically by angle-resolved Mie scattering. Under acoustic agitation, irradiation raised retention in eleven of twelve paired comparisons, at every concentration, by 0.17 on average against a measured aliquot-to-aliquot scatter of 0.02; the twelfth comparison lies within that scatter. Under stirring, which already keeps most particles suspended, it produces no resolvable change. The angular positions of the Mie maxima are unchanged to within about 1% over 3 h, so the particles are neither fragmented nor aggregated and the effect arises from particle transport rather than from changes in the particles. An order-of-magnitude analysis rules out optical forces, the optical Kerr effect, and transient photochemistry, and leaves laser-driven convection: the power absorbed by the water sustains flows orders of magnitude faster than the 1.8 um/s settling velocity. Femtosecond irradiation therefore acts as a non-contact, supplementary agitation source, most effective where mechanical mixing is weak.

item.title: Functional Superoscillations in a Wave Processor
item.description: arXiv:2610.34111v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Physical wave processors are constrained by diffraction, but the bandwidth of the mathematical functions they implement need not be set by it. Here, we demonstrate continuous and multiplexed optical processing of superoscillatory functions, in which a scalar argument is encoded onto a wavefront and a fixed diffractive wave processor synthesizes optical responses that approximate the corresponding function outputs in parallel. Unlike conventional superoscillatory optics that generates predetermined fields, superoscillation here is expressed in the input-output dependence on the encoded argument. Its frequencies are therefore distinct from the transverse spatial frequencies of propagating light and are not subject to the same diffraction-imposed cutoff. We demonstrate complex-valued superoscillatory function synthesis and introduce a multiplexed architecture that simultaneously evaluates distinct target superoscillatory functions whose harmonic content exceeds that of the optical input encoding. Visible-light experiments further validate this beyond-encoding superoscillatory regime. Together, these results establish functional superoscillation as a design principle for wave-based computation and show how interference, diffractive depth and spatial channel allocation extend the functional reach of passive wave processors. More broadly, these analyses establish a separation between functional bandwidth and physical wave bandwidth in analog optical computation.

item.title: Amplitude-Dependent Damping of Gravity--Capillary Waves in Power-Law Fluids: An Energy-Dissipation Framework
item.description: arXiv:2610.34351v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Classical gravity--capillary theory locates the restoring-force crossover, but the wave amplitudes and depths for which energy losses remain measurable depend on the constitutive response and on where viscous dissipation occurs. We develop a weak-loss mechanical-energy model for small-steepness progressive surface waves in memoryless power--law liquids. The full invariant of the leading inviscid strain field yields the deep-water bulk law $\dd A/\dd t=-C_tA^n$, with $C_t=4Kk^2(2k\Omega)^{n-1}/[(n+1)\rho]$, and the corresponding spatial law $\dd A/\dd x=-(C_t/v_g)A^n$. For finite depth we calculate bulk dissipation using a phase- and depth-resolved quadrature $J_n(kh)$ and formulate a separate oscillatory power--law bottom layer. We solve the latter numerically in periodic state, obtaining dimensionless integrated wall losses $I_{0.6}\simeq0.5432$ and $I_{1.4}\simeq0.4708$ and recovering the exact Newtonian benchmark $I_1=1/2$. These values make it possible to evaluate conditional finite-depth bulk--wall dominance boundaries rather than only their amplitude exponents. The theory is organized into restoring-force, attenuation, local propagation-length, and dissipation-mechanism regime maps; at fixed wave steepness it additionally predicts a capillary-side maximum of normalized temporal damping for $0<n<2/3$. Grid, time-step, domain, and energy-work checks support the reduced wall calculation, while the coupled bulk--wall approximation still requires independent free-surface numerical or experimental validation. The results provide a reproducible single-fluid reference for subsequent two-liquid interfacial-wave modeling.

item.title: 华为将韬定律思想引入基站设计，发布新一代移动通信网产品及解决方案
item.description: IT之家 10 月 27 日现场消息，华为今日在上海练秋湖研发中心举行 Decoding China 2026 活动，发布新一代 移动通信网产品及解决方案。 华为公司副总裁、无线网络业务管理委员会主任方向介绍，通信方式的每次升级，都会推动社会发展质的飞跃。AI 从数字世界走向物理世界，联接规模不断扩大；智能业务也走向全终端、全业务、全场景。 方向认为，AI 业务改变了流量结构，对网络上行体验和容量提出了更高要求， 网络需求从下行为主走向上下行并重 。 根据梅特卡夫定律，网络价值与用户数量的平方成正比。IT之家在现场了解到，方向认为， 新一代通信网的价值还需要加上一个影响因素 —— 平均联接质量 ，联接的价值不仅取决于联接的数量，更取决于联接的质量。 方向展示了华为的新一代移动通信网基站设备 Huawei VitaAAU ，首次将 RetinaMIMO 引入 U6GHz 设备，并首次实现极简绿色架构。 IT之家注：U6GHz（Upper 6GHz）指 6GHz 上半频段 ，具备较大连续频宽潜力。 VitaAAU 是面向 U6GHz 频段的有源天线单元，可理解为 Sub-6GHz 频段 MetaAAU 的下一代。其核心技术 RetinaMIMO 以“ 百通道 × 千阵子 × 高速扫描系统 ”为特点，三大能力分别为 256TRx、1500+ 天线阵子（AEs）及 HBF 高速波束扫描技术，旨在更有效地管理波束和频谱资源，探索更大网络容量与更佳服务能力。 Huawei VitaAAU 目前已开启全球商用 ，支持大带宽构筑 10Gbps 峰值体验，已落地阿联酋、中国香港、中国澳门等。 此外， 华为还将韬定律思想引入基站设计 ，让网络像一个小区，实现微缩系统级求解、降低求解时延，实现性能跃升。

item.description: IT之家 10 月 27 日消息，Intel（英特尔）目前正在准备桌面端和移动端的 "Raptor Lake Next" 处理器作为既有平台的小幅更新。第三方海关舱单记录平台纽佰德 (NBD) 已经记录到了多条相关记录。 当前发现的记录集中于 8 月 18~19 两日，采购地均为越南，货物描述中均提到了 "FCLGA>"（ 更有可能是桌面端的产品 ）。以下是 4 款涉及的处理器的已知信息： 代号 缓存 频率 99DLMT 33MB 2.1GHz 99DLMV 30MB 3.5GHz 99DLMX 24MB 2.6GHz 99DLMW 24MB 2.4GHz 这些处理器的标注频率都相对较低，该数据应该指的是性能核基本频率，其中频率不到 3GHz 的 "99DLMT" "99DLMV" "99DLMW" 很可能是 65W 型号，"99DLMV" 则有可能是 125W 产品。 33MB 缓存的 "99DLMT" 应该是 8P + 12E 结构，30MB 缓存的 "99DLMV" 很可能是 8P + 8E 的产品，"99DLMV" 与 "99DLMW" 定位则更低。

item.title: 华强北商家称近期内存价格回调但仍居高位，市场“有价无市”、10 月销量普遍下滑 20% 至 30%
item.description: IT之家 10 月 27 日消息，据央视财经今日报道，近段时间，A 股存储板块持续出现调整，多家龙头公司股价较年内高点回撤明显，部分公司回撤幅度超过 40%。 记者走访广东深圳华强北多家内存柜台发现，目前 16G DDR5 内存条报价普遍在 1400 元至 1600 元，32G 在 2000 元至 3000 多元，1T 固态硬盘 800 元至 1000 多元。 华强北商家表示，近期内存价格相比前期高点， 的确出现了回调，但是幅度都不大 ，16G、32G 内存条分别下跌 20 元到 50 元，1T 硬盘跌 20 元到 30 元，整体内存价格仍居高位。 报道还称，目前内存销量比价格波动更加明显，走访中多位商家反映， 10 月份以来他们的销量普遍下滑 20% 至 30% ，整个内存流通渠道甚至出现了价格倒挂的情况。 目前内存出厂价仍然在涨，但是由于不少渠道商前期囤了很多货，而大部分消费者在内存价格高企的时刻选择观望，整个市场需求下滑，为了迅速回笼资金减轻库存压力，不少渠道商还是会选择降价出货。 业内人士表示，内存市场价格出现小幅下调， 主要是有些渠道商资金压力大，必须出货回笼资金，但大家都是高成本进货，谁也不敢降太多 ，于是市场出现了报价坚挺、成交冷清、局部倒挂的现象，整个渠道库存和资金压力正在累积。

item.title: 国家广电总局：交互式网络电视 IPTV 应实现开机看全屏直播功能，不得播放开机广告
item.description: IT之家 10 月 27 日消息，国家广播电视总局今日发布公告，《 交互式网络电视运营服务管理暂行规定 》（下称《规定》）已经于 2026 年 10 月 23 日国家广播电视总局局务会议审议通过，现予公布，自 2026 年 11 月 27 日起施行。 该《规定》所称交互式网络电视（英文简称 IPTV）运营服务，是指依法设立的交互式网络电视集成播控服务提供者和传输服务提供者，利用交互式网络电视专网直接或者间接向个人用户、家庭用户、集团用户等提供广播电视服务的活动。 《规定》要求交互式网络电视集成播控服务提供者在页面显著位置展示“中国 IPTV-省份”的呼号等播出标识。 IT之家注意到，《规定》提到，交互式网络电视集成播控服务提供者应当坚持直播优先原则， 实现开机看全屏直播功能，设置频道回看入口，不得播放开机广告 。智能电视机应支持优先呈现直播频道功能，提供便捷设置入口。 此外，交互式网络电视集成播控服务提供者应当向用户提供便捷设置入口， 方便用户自行选择开机进直播或者电视交互主页 。电视交互主页的页面、导航栏、状态栏、推荐位等内容应当符合国务院广播电视主管部门相关要求。 交互式网络电视集成播控服务提供者应当在交互式网络电视首页 设立免费专区 ，对优质免费内容进行重点推荐，精简收费栏目数量，明示节目收费信息，规范应用专区运营和订购支付管理。 交互式网络电视集成播控服务提供者和传输服务提供者应当简化遥控操作， 实现遥控器一键切换直播信源 。
